_schema.question: the query to run
_schema.answerable: false = the corpus cannot answer this; correct behaviour is abstention (empty retrieval)
_schema.tier: a | b — must match the document's tier in eval/corpus/MANIFEST.yaml. Metrics are reported per tier and never averaged
_schema.category: plain-fact | table-answer | ocr-answer | multi-hop | cross-doc | long-table-tail | conversational | unanswerable
_schema.expected_sources: files (basenames) a relevant chunk must come from
_schema.expected_keywords: a retrieved chunk counts as relevant if its source matches AND any keyword appears (case-insensitive); empty list = source match alone suffices
_schema.answer_snippet: VERBATIM text from the source document that answers the question. Required for answerable entries. It defines the lexical-overlap slice, so it must be copied from the document, never from retrieval output
_schema.history: optional prior turns [{question, answer}] seeded into session memory in full mode; drives the needs_rewrite() branch
_schema.expects_rewrite: the needs_rewrite() verdict this entry must produce. A mismatch FAILS the eval run — that is how a widened anaphora regex is caught before it silently rewrites standalone questions
_schema.full_mode_only: true = this entry REQUIRES history-based query rewriting, which only full mode performs. Retrieval mode sends the question to the retriever verbatim, so failing there is the mode behaving correctly, not a defect. Excluded from retrieval-mode metrics; still reported in its category slice.
_schema.requires_document: optional list of corpus documents that must be INDEXED for this entry to mean what it was written to mean. Defaults to expected_sources. State it explicitly when an unanswerable entry's difficulty depends on a document being present to be confused with. run_eval.py drops entries whose required documents carry ingest: false in MANIFEST.yaml.
